title: Geometry Skia cannot emit as axis-aligned quads costs ~10ms/frame, however little of it there is
symptom: The reference machine (Ryzen 7 5800 / RTX 4060 Ti / Chrome 151 / X11) held 51fps idle, 49 in combat, 44 with the automap open, with ~30% of frames landing on exactly 33.4ms (two vsyncs). Engine busy time was 6.1-6.5ms p50 throughout — the cost is entirely outside the measured phases.
culprit: Chrome's GPU-process canvas rasteriser batches rect fills and image blits into one quad stream. Geometry it cannot express that way needs a coverage pass, which flushes the batch and resolves the render target; with ~2,600 quads plus a full-canvas putImageData already pending, that flush misses the vsync deadline (CrGpuMain 99.7% saturated; RasterDecoderImpl::DoEndRasterCHROMIUM mean 10.9ms). The penalty is fixed per frame and independent of count and of position in the op stream: one arc fill costs as much as sixty-four. IN the class: path fills/strokes (arc+fill, polygon fill, line stroke) and strokeRect drawn while lineJoin is 'round' (1 call = 48.0fps vs 59.0 with miter). NOT in the class, all verified by injection on a clean frame: plain miter-joined strokeRect (free at 24/frame, any size/alignment/lineWidth/position), strokeText (free at 8/frame), fillRect (3,000 extra are free), drawImage, and an axis-aligned rect clip().
refactor: Pre-render every per-frame path glyph once into a detached offscreen canvas (rotating ones into a 128-step rotation atlas, so no live rotate() either) and blit it; rasterise lines as fillRect runs, circles as a scaled disc sprite, and scanline-fillable silhouettes (the flame jet) row by row; route every rect outline through outlineRect. Partial fixes buy nothing — the penalty is per frame. Note a glyph pre-renders on a detached context that inherits no state (lineJoin, lineCap, imageSmoothingEnabled), so anything the shape depends on must be set inside its own draw.
evidence: In-situ attribution by suppressing canvas method classes at the CanvasRenderingContext2D prototype on the live game; CDP devtools.timeline trace; before/after with the same probe, 8s per cell
outcomeNote: FIXED 2026-08-02 across three commits: the four always-on sites, then the combat effects/automap/rings, then the toasts and lore overlay. Final measurement, original -> final: idle 51.3 -> 59.1fps (dropped 70/411 -> 7/473), combat 48.8 -> 58.0 (90/391 -> 15/464), automap-open 44.3 -> 58.6 (126/354 -> 11/469), automap-closed 47.9 -> 59.6 (96/384 -> 3/477). Every 'suppress all path/stroke' control cell is within noise of as-shipped. outlineRect re-justified by stubbing it back to ctx.strokeRect: idle 48.8 / combat 48.1 / automap-closed 45.5, a ~10fps regression, so it stays. THREE ROUNDS OF WRONG MECHANISM before this landed: the report first cleared strokeRect on synthetic evidence, then indicted it wholesale on an in-situ revert, and only the third round found lineJoin='round' as the actual trigger — see doc/dev/perf-review-2026-08-02.md for the full retraction.

title: The benchmark harness could not see this class of bug — twice over
symptom: A regression costing ~10ms/frame and 30% of frames ran undetected, and the 2026-07 audit closed it as 'environmental'. Both of the harness's defaults were the reason.
culprit: (a) `busy` measures the time to RECORD canvas draw calls; rasterising that display list happens afterwards in the GPU process, and busy cannot see it — busy was 6.1ms p50 both broken and fixed. (b) The harness prefers headless, and headless Chromium rasterises the canvas in software where the coverage-pass penalty does not exist: every scenario reads a flat 60fps with zero dropped frames there regardless of what the renderer does.
refactor: Add a presented-frame metric (dropped-frame count/pct, frame period derived from the run's own median rather than assuming 60Hz, dropped = interval >= 1.5 periods) alongside busy; lead the per-run console line with it; tag it `[HEADLESS — cannot see raster cost]` and print a startup warning when headless so the number can never be quoted without the caveat; surface it in the HTML report; rewrite performance.md's 'prefer headless' guidance.
evidence: Same build, same scenario, 30s apart: headed 59.4fps 7/713 dropped, headless 60.0fps 0/600 dropped, busy 6.60ms in both
outcomeNote: DONE 2026-08-02. Presented-frame metric threaded through run JSON, per-run console output, calibration and the HTML report (older runs lacking the field render 'n/a' rather than crashing, matching the existing newer-schema fallback convention). Headless startup warning added. performance.md now documents both metrics, the headless blind spot with the demonstration table above, and reframes the 'headed measures the desktop too' gotcha that produced the wrong 2026-07 conclusion.

title: No guard against reintroducing expensive canvas geometry
symptom: The expensive case is invisible at the call site: `ctx.strokeRect(...)` is free or costs a quarter of the frame budget depending on a `lineJoin` set by whatever drew before it, and `drawWeapon` sets exactly that. Nothing about a regression would look wrong in review, in a unit test, or in the headless harness.
refactor: A Vitest case asserting no per-frame renderer issues fill()/stroke()/strokeRect() on the scene canvas, exercised on the pre-rendered fast path (stub an offscreen context that actually paints so pathSprites' probe passes) — otherwise it tests the direct-draw fallback, which is supposed to use paths, and passes vacuously.
evidence: Verified red: injecting a raw ctx.strokeRect into drawHud fails with the call count, call site and suggested replacement
outcomeNote: DONE 2026-08-02: src/engine/renderCost.test.ts, 9 cases covering all 7 weapon viewmodels x flash x recoil, minimap, compass, automap, HUD, crosshair, every toast and banner, all combat effects, and every world-billboard collector. First assertion checks the fast path is actually engaged, so the guard cannot pass vacuously.

title: An axis-aligned rect clip() is free — unlike every other path call
symptom: drawAutomap's beginPath/rect/clip was on P1's fix list as site 8, on the assumption that every path call carries the per-frame coverage-pass penalty.
culprit: None. Skia takes a rectangular clip as a scissor rectangle, not a coverage mask, so it never leaves the batched-quad path.
refactor: No action. Measured after the automap's player-marker triangle was converted: 59.0fps with the clip still in place vs 58.6 with it suppressed — within noise, and the automap's whole deficit turned out to be the triangle. Non-rectangular clips were NOT tested and must not be assumed to share this.
evidence: scenarios probe, automap-open cell, as-shipped vs path/stroke-suppressed after the P1 round-2 fix
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-08-02: rect clip kept as-is by measurement.

title: WebKit renders the raycaster 4-5x slower than Chromium
symptom: In WebKit the idle scene alone costs ~23ms busy per frame (raycast-walls 19.1ms vs 4.2ms in Chromium, hud 4.2ms vs 0.7ms) — under 30fps before any combat happens; 336 slow frames in 3x30s vs 0 in Chromium.
culprit: The per-column pipeline (640 one-pixel-wide drawImage blits + fillRect overlays per frame) and per-frame fillText HUD are drastically more expensive in WebKit's canvas implementation. Caveat: measured in headless WebKit (possibly software-rendered); real Safari with GPU acceleration may be faster — needs one verification run on real hardware.
refactor: For WebKit (feature-detect), render walls into the same ImageData buffer the floor-caster already uses (pure typed-array writes + one putImageData) instead of per-column drawImage; cache static HUD text to an offscreen canvas. Alternatively: document Safari as degraded until verified on real hardware.
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-07-18 (user decision): no Safari verification, no WebKit-specific rendering work — WebKit isn't a supported target worth the investment. Headless-WebKit numbers stay in the report as documentation; if a real Safari user ever reports slowness, the ImageData wall-render refactor sketched above is the known lever.

title: Minimap redraws every wall tile of the whole map, every frame
symptom: The hud phase grows with map area even when nothing on the minimap changed: 0.72ms on an 84x84 demo map vs 1.10ms on the 160x160 magento2 map (idle, minimap showing — the default HUD state). Extrapolates linearly: a 250x250 monster file costs ~2.5ms/frame just for the corner minimap.
culprit: renderMinimap's nested for-y/for-x loop issues one fillRect per wall tile over the entire grid every frame, plus per-category marker loops — O(map area) canvas calls for an image that only changes when doors/secrets open or entities move.
refactor: Render the static wall layer to an offscreen canvas once per level (invalidate on gridVersion bump — doors/secret walls already increment it), then per frame drawImage that cache + draw only the dynamic markers (player/enemies/pickups).
evidence: hud phase medians across s1 (84x84) vs s4 (160x160) baselines, 2026-07-18T00-13/09-05 runs
outcomeNote: FIXED 2026-07-18: walls cached to an offscreen canvas keyed on (map, gridVersion, cell). Measured: hud phase 0.72->0.10ms (demo), 1.09->0.24ms (160x160 magento2).

title: Wall-edge antialiasing is affordable — it could ship enabled
symptom: WALL_EDGE_ANTIALIASING_ENABLED is off by default awaiting cost data. Measured: no detectable busy-time cost on the demo scene (5.60 vs 5.70ms, below the 0.2ms detection floor) and +0.4ms/frame on the 160x160 magento2 map. No frame-interval regression in either.
culprit: The feared per-column extra fillRect + shadedTexel cost is real but small in Chromium; it scales with wall-column count, hence the modest magento2 delta.
refactor: Flip the flag on by default (Chromium/Firefox). If WebKit's canvas slowness (F23) is confirmed on real Safari, gate it off there via the same feature-detect.
evidence: Interleaved A/B, 5+5 runs per scenario, perf_runs/2026-07-18T01-01-33-870Z
outcomeNote: DONE 2026-07-18: flag flipped ON by default (commit aed956e) — default-behavior test updated, docs/changelog reworded, smoothed silhouettes verified via real-browser screenshot.

title: Distance fog ('farther = darker') is free — keep it
symptom: User asked whether the fog effect slows rendering. Measured via a purpose-built DISTANCE_FOG_ENABLED A/B: fog-off saves under 0.1ms/frame on both the demo scene (4.90 vs 4.80) and the magento2 map (5.50 vs 5.40) — below the 0.2ms detection floor.
culprit: None — the 640 per-column alpha fillRects and the floor caster's per-pixel multiply batch efficiently in Chromium.
refactor: No action. Keep the flag (one-line toggle) for future per-browser measurements; it is also the mechanism that would cheaply confirm F23's attribution on real Safari.
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-07-18: no action needed by measurement — fog stays on; the DISTANCE_FOG_ENABLED flag remains for future per-browser A/Bs.

title: pathField full-map reflood: hypothesis refuted at real map sizes
symptom: Static analysis flagged the O(map-area) BFS reflood on every player tile-crossing as a prime magento2 framedrop suspect. Measured with continuous noclip movement on the 160x160 map: busy median identical to standing still (5.50 vs 5.50ms); the sim phase rises only 0.11 -> 0.16ms.
culprit: The flat Int32Array BFS is simply fast — a 25.6k-tile reflood every ~150ms amortizes to ~0.05ms/frame. Preallocated buffers mean no GC pressure either.
refactor: None needed at current map scales. If maps ever grow past ~500x500, revisit with an incremental/dirty-region flood.
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-07-18: hypothesis refuted by measurement, no code change warranted at current map scales.

title: Console-sidebar DOM mirroring: no measurable frame cost at real log rates
symptom: Static analysis rated the per-console.log DOM append + scrollTop layout flush as a High combat-time cost. Measured (sustained fire on the 280-enemy map, sidebar active vs bypassed): busy p95/p99/max and heap slopes are indistinguishable across 5+5 interleaved runs.
culprit: Real combat emits a few logs per second, not the tens-per-frame the static estimate assumed; at that rate the layout flush is noise.
refactor: Optional hygiene: defer the scrollTop assignment to one rAF callback per batch of appends. Worth doing only if a future feature raises log frequency by an order of magnitude.
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-07-18: hypothesis refuted at real log rates, no code change; optional rAF-batched scrollTop noted for the future.

title: Constant per-frame allocation churn (buildStats, captureSnapshot, gamepad copy)
symptom: Every frame allocates: a ~20-field computeScore input + ~10-field result + ownedWeapons Set spread (buildStats, even while paused), an 18-field input snapshot + filtered array (captureSnapshot — evaluated before the ?. can short-circuit, so it runs with no recorder attached), and an Array.from copy of the gamepad list. Measured heap churn during combat: ~0.3MB/s with periodic GC; no measurable frame-time effect in 30s captures on this 32GB machine.
culprit: Argument evaluation before optional-chaining (engine.ts:1042), unmemoized computeScore call in buildStats (engine.ts:2322), Array.from(getGamepads()) (input.ts:428).
refactor: Three cheap, safe fixes: guard the record call with if (this.replayRecorder), memoize computeScore on its input signature, iterate the gamepad list without copying. Primarily lowers GC pressure on memory-constrained machines — the plausible profile of the Task 241 reporter's environment.
evidence: Static audit + heap slopes in s4 fire runs; 10-min soak in perf_runs (2026-07-18, s2 600s run)
outcomeNote: PARTIALLY FIXED 2026-07-18: captureSnapshot now guarded (only allocates with a recorder attached), gamepad list no longer copied per frame. computeScore memoization dropped as inapplicable — levelTimeSec is a real input (speed bonus), the score legitimately changes every frame; remaining churn accepted (measured Low).

title: Replay viewer produces garbage ?perfDebug=1 phase logs
symptom: Watching a replay with ?perfDebug=1 logs monotonically growing phase times (seconds-scale 'busy' per frame) — any future perf capture taken during replay playback is unusable without external correction.
culprit: The replay rAF loop calls engine.advance() directly and never calls perf.beginFrame(), so FramePerfLogger's per-frame phase map is never reset.
refactor: Have the replay loop call a small public engine.beginPerfFrame(rawDtMs) wrapper (or fold beginFrame into advance() using a stashed rawDt). The benchmark harness currently works around it by differencing.
evidence: Discovered by the harness: S2 busy(med)=6955ms; verified against replay-loop code
outcomeNote: FIXED 2026-07-18: perf-frame begin moved into advance() itself (frame() hands over the unclamped delta; direct drivers fall back to their own dt) — replay viewer and headless drivers now produce correct ?perfDebug=1 phases.

title: Task 241 (magento2 120->30fps): not reproducible as engine cost — evidence points environmental
symptom: The reported drop could not be reproduced in any of 6 magento2 scenarios (idle / look / sustained fire / dry-fire / mousemove-flood / continuous movement, 160x160 map, 280 enemies): engine busy never exceeded ~13ms worst-frame, medians ~5.6ms. In headed desktop sessions, slow frames DID appear — but every single one was a missed vsync with ~27ms unaccounted and normal (~5ms) game phases, i.e. stalls outside game code; headless runs of identical scenarios show zero slow frames.
culprit: Most plausible: the reporter's compositor/GPU path (disabled hardware acceleration, large high-DPI upscale of the 640x400 canvas, 120Hz display doubling compositor deadlines), extensions, or memory-pressure GC — not raycaster/AI/pathfinding CPU. The mousemove-flood test also weakens the high-poll-mouse theory (no effect at ~2000 events/s).
refactor: Sharpen the ?perfDebug=1 capture request to the reporter: have them include the [perf] env: line and a few SLOW lines — if their SLOW frames show small phases + large unacct (matching our headed pattern), direct them to chrome://gpu (hardware acceleration), window size/DPR, and extensions rather than waiting on engine optimizations. The F7+F10 allocation fixes are the only engine-side lever that plausibly helps a memory-constrained machine.
evidence: All s4-* cells across perf_runs/2026-07-18T00-13 (headed) and 09-05..09-47 (headless); slow-frame phase attributions
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-08-23: the reporter confirms the lag is gone. Never reproduced locally (no 120Hz panel here); the 8.33ms-budget argument stood in for a repro and held up in the field. Which change fixed it was never established — he may have been on Classic (u32 floor-cast only) or Sharp (which also pairs the half-res floor), and a Chrome update on his side is not excluded. See doc/dev/history.md.

title: RESPONSIVE_CANVAS_SCALING: no engine-side cost; compositor cost unverified
symptom: A/B shows zero busy-time difference (5.00 vs 5.00 idle; replay identical). The flag's real risk — compositor upscale cost of a larger on-screen canvas — is not observable headless, and the headed attempt was invalidated by desktop throttling.
culprit: Engine work is resolution-independent (fixed 640x400 internal canvas); only the browser's scale-and-composite step grows.
refactor: Safe to enable from the engine's perspective. Before shipping, do one attended headed spot-check (fps overlay on, window maximized) — the harness cell exists (--flag scaling), it just needs an unlocked screen.
outcomeNote: VERIFIED on-screen 2026-07-18 (user-attended headed A/B, 5+5 interleaved runs): busy median 6.70 vs 6.70ms, intervals/p95/slow-counts identical — compositor upscale is free at desktop window sizes. Safe to enable whenever the resizing behavior itself is wanted; perf is no longer a blocker. ENABLED by default 2026-07-18 (commit 183ec87), live-verified at 1920x1080 + runtime resize.

title: Bundle and startup are healthy
symptom: Cold-cache first-interactive payload is ~17KB gzipped (HTML+CSS+main JS 101KB gz parses in ~200ms on mid-range hardware); all 18 tree-sitter wasm grammars (2.9MB gz total) and the 223KB default-highscore replay load lazily on first use. No render-blocking resources.
culprit: None — build-time-fetch + per-language lazy loading is working as designed.
refactor: Optional: code-split the replay system out of the main bundle (~10-15% startup parse win). Not recommended now — architectural churn for a page that is already fast.
evidence: dist/ size table + startup flow analysis (static audit D)
outcomeNote: CLOSED 2026-07-18: healthy by measurement; optional replay-system code-split noted, deliberately not taken.

title: PLAYER_STATS_ENABLED: the level-end stats screen was disabled on a claim nobody measured
symptom: The player-facing stats rows on Commit Summary / Kernel Panic / Build Successful never appeared in real play. Disabled at birth 2026-07-17 on the claim that the ~20 per-event record* sites 'measurably slowed gameplay down'.
culprit: No measurement was ever recorded for that claim - not in the commit, not in history.md, not in this file. It stood for five weeks and was cited as precedent in decisions.md.
impact: Low (perf) / Medium (product): a shipped feature was withheld, and the accuracy score bonus - up to 250 points a level - was silently always zero, since it divides by a shot count telemetry never recorded.
refactor: Flip the const. Route the off case through ?ablate=telemetry so the ~45 now-unreachable guard branches stay testable, rather than ignoring them.
evidence: Two A/Bs, neither reproducing a cost. 2026-08-02 (perf-review section 7): sim phase 0.1ms of 16.7ms either way, but on a pre-P1 build already dropping ~29% of frames. 2026-08-23 remeasure on a build holding the vsync edge: clock-equalized c2-2bg, 4 runs/arm, headed - busy median 5.775ms off vs 5.800ms on (+0.025ms) against a 0.16ms calibrated floor; dropped frames fell 1.72%->1.57%; longTasks 0 both arms. Level-end derivation measured directly (one-shot, engine already stopped): 0.00027ms, 0.0016% of a frame.
outcomeNote: SHIPPED ON 2026-08-23. Harness gained --flag playerstats so this is reproducible rather than a throwaway probe. The s2-replay boundary cell was attempted and abandoned: it could not produce comparable arms, so the level-end cost was measured directly instead.
